Pregnant Georgia woman rescued by first responders after going into labor during Helene
Anchor/Reporter
A pregnant Georgia woman was rescued by first responders early Friday morning as Helene brought deadly impacts to the state.
Statesboro Chief of Police Mike Broadhead said the woman went into labor around 5 a.m. as dangerous winds and rain were lashing the area.
Advertisement
She called 911 and police were able to escort an ambulance around downed power lines and trees to bring the woman to East Georgia Medical Center.
People were urged to remain indoors as the worst of the weather continues to pass through.
